h2: Aerospace NDT around Chicago: the Rockford cluster, wide-body MRO and what suppliers must document
html:
Aerospace NDT around Chicago: the Rockford cluster, wide-body MRO and what suppliers must document

Most aerospace NDT in the Chicago region happens northwest of the city around Rockford, where engine fuel systems, gears and aircraft systems are built and wide-body airliners are heavily maintained. Atlantis supports those programmes with ASNT NDT Level III procedure and written-practice work, inspection mobilised under the customer's specification, and NAS 410 Level 3 services delivered through an associate.

The manufacturing base. More than 70 aerospace supply-chain companies operate in the Rockford area, employing about 7,000 people, and the wider cluster reaching into Chicago and southeastern Wisconsin counts more than 200. Woodward's Loves Park plant, opened in the middle of the last decade, produces fuel systems for jet engines. Collins Aerospace operates in Rockford, the former headquarters city of Sundstrand, which United Technologies combined with Hamilton Standard in 1999 to form Hamilton Sundstrand, a lineage that now sits within Collins Aerospace. Forest City Gear in nearby Roscoe has supplied gears for NASA's Mars rovers. Fuel-system components and castings typically see fluorescent penetrant and radiography; precision gears and shafts see magnetic particle inspection; machined parts see eddy current and ultrasonic checks.

Maintenance, repair and overhaul. AAR Corp. is headquartered in Wood Dale and opened an airframe MRO at Chicago Rockford International Airport in December 2016, with hangar space for wide-body aircraft. Heavy checks of that kind typically rely on eddy current around fasteners, ultrasonic corrosion and bond checks, and visual inspection to the OEM's NDT manual, all under the repair station's FAA approval. O'Hare and Midway handled 867,635 and 253,046 flights respectively in 2016, according to FAA figures cited by Air Cargo Update, and line maintenance at airports of that size generates its own inspection demand between heavy checks.

Inspection that Atlantis mobilises for an aerospace customer is performed at the customer's plant or hangar, to the customer's process specification and acceptance criteria, by technicians whose certification the customer has reviewed. Where the specification demands NAS 410 personnel, that requirement is confirmed at quotation rather than assumed.

The documents an aerospace NDT supplier near Chicago is audited on:

  • A written practice to NAS 410 or EN 4179, with Level 3 responsibilities named, which differs from the SNT-TC-1A structure most industrial firms use.
  • Process control to ASTM E1417 for penetrant and ASTM E1444 for magnetic particle, plus any prime contractor's own specification.
  • Nadcap accreditation where the customer requires it, and records that cite the specification revision applied to each part.

Where Atlantis fits. For suppliers running SNT-TC-1A programmes, an ASNT NDT Level III can author procedures, review technique sheets and prepare for customer audits through aerospace NDT consulting and procedure development. NAS 410 Level 3 duties are handled through an associate, never by Atlantis staff. For composite and bonded structure, laser shearography and infrared thermography can be mobilised for disbond and impact-damage surveys. Atlantis's own courses follow SNT-TC-1A, not NAS 410; the aerospace NDT training page explains how that difference affects a candidate. Certification records can be held in Atlantis ERP certificate tracking.

To discuss an aerospace scope in Rockford or Chicago, describe the part, specification and method.
